title: 3D NAND Inspection - Missing Pattern Detection on Archer 750
subtitle: Post-Metallization Quality Validation for 7nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Anna Petrova

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Archer 750 system to detect and classify Missing Pattern defects during post-metallization inspection at the 7nm technology node. The test is conducted at Chandler Fab 42 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Missing Pattern defects that are critical to yield at the 7nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Archer 750 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Archer 750
- Inspection Type: 3D NAND Inspection
- Target Defect: Missing Pattern
- Process Step: Post-Metallization
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 7nm
- Fab Location: Chandler Fab 42

This test case applies to all Archer 750 systems deployed at Chandler Fab 42 for post-metallization monitoring in the 7nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Archer 750
Software Version: v12.8.310
Recipe: 3D_NAND_INSPECTION_7nm_POST_METALLIZATION
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: High (65 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.5μm
Edge Exclusion: 3mm
Sampling Plan: 21-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Archer 750 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the '3D NAND Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Missing Pattern defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 7nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 94 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 91% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±0.6% for 3D NAND Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.98 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-04-09
Wafers Tested: 22
Total Defects Found: 2472
Defect Density: 786.86 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 3.4%
Capture Rate: 93.7%
Test Duration: 199 minutes
System Uptime: 99.0%

Result Classification: NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Archer 750 demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Missing Pattern at the 7nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) No significant drift was observed during the test duration.

e) Recipe portability between systems at this fab was confirmed.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
